('O(n)', 'O(1)', 'medium', 'r0-r7').source:
IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Handle base cases
    JZ R0, BASE0
    MOV R1, 1
    JZ R1, BASE1    ; never taken, just placeholder
    ; Check if n == 1
    MOV R2, 1
    JZ R0, BASE0
    ; compare n with 1
    MOV R3, R0
    SUB R3, 1
    JZ R3, BASE1

    ; General case: compute fib(n) iteratively
    ; R1 = fib(i-1) = 0 (fib(0))
    ; R2 = fib(i)   = 1 (fib(1))
    ; R3 = counter, starts at 1, goes up to n-1
    ; MOD = 1000000007

    MOV R1, 0       ; fib(0)
    MOV R2, 1       ; fib(1)
    MOV R3, 1       ; counter = 1
    MOV R4, 1000000007  ; modulus

LOOP:
    JGE R3, R0, DONE   ; if counter >= n, done
    ; R5 = R1 + R2
    MOV R5, R1
    ADD R5, R2
    MOD R5, R4
    ; shift: R1 = R2, R2 = R5
    MOV R1, R2
    MOV R2, R5
    INC R3
    JMP LOOP

DONE:
    OUT R2
    HALT

BASE0:
    OUT 0
    HALT

BASE1:
    OUT 1
    HALT

('O(n)', 'O(n)', 'medium', 'r0-r7').source:
IN R0
    MOV R4, 1000000007

    ; Store fib values in memory
    ; mem[0] = fib(0) = 0
    ; mem[1] = fib(1) = 1
    ; mem[i] = (mem[i-1] + mem[i-2]) % MOD

    MOV R1, 0
    STOR R1, [R1+0]   ; mem[0] = 0
    MOV R2, 1
    STOR R2, [R2+0]   ; mem[1] = 1 (address 1)

    ; Check if n <= 1
    MOV R3, 1
    JLE R0, R3, SMALL

    ; R5 = current index, starts at 2
    MOV R5, 2

FILL:
    JGT R5, R0, READ_ANS
    ; mem[R5] = (mem[R5-1] + mem[R5-2]) % MOD
    MOV R6, R5
    SUB R6, 1
    LOAD R1, [R6+0]   ; fib(i-1)
    MOV R6, R5
    SUB R6, 2
    LOAD R2, [R6+0]   ; fib(i-2)
    ADD R1, R2
    MOD R1, R4
    STOR R1, [R5+0]
    INC R5
    JMP FILL

READ_ANS:
    LOAD R7, [R0+0]
    OUT R7
    HALT

SMALL:
    ; n is 0 or 1, load directly
    LOAD R7, [R0+0]
    OUT R7
    HALT

('O(log n)', 'O(log n)', 'large', 'r0-r7.source:
; Fast doubling Fibonacci using explicit stack in memory
; fib(2k)   = fib(k) * (2*fib(k+1) - fib(k))
; fib(2k+1) = fib(k)^2 + fib(k+1)^2
; Stack stores the sequence of bits (0=even, 1=odd) of n
; Then we apply doubling formulas bottom-up

IN R0
MOV R6, 1000000007

; Base cases
JZ R0, OUT_ZERO
MOV R7, 1
JLE R0, R7, OUT_ONE

; Push bits of n onto stack in memory starting at address 200
; We push 0 if n is even, 1 if n is odd, then n = n/2, repeat until n=0
; Stack pointer in R7, starts at 200
MOV R7, 200
MOV R3, R0

PUSH_LOOP:
    JZ R3, PUSH_DONE
    MOV R4, R3
    MOD R4, 2          ; R4 = R3 % 2 (bit)
    STOR R4, [R7+0]
    INC R7
    DIV R3, 2
    JMP PUSH_LOOP

PUSH_DONE:
; Now pop bits and apply fast doubling
; R1 = a = fib(k), R2 = b = fib(k+1), start with k=0: a=0, b=1
MOV R1, 0
MOV R2, 1

; R7 points one past top of stack, decrement to read
POP_LOOP:
    MOV R5, 200
    JLE R7, R5, RESULT  ; if R7 <= 200, stack empty

    DEC R7
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]     ; R4 = bit

    ; Doubling step:
    ; c = a * (2*b - a) % MOD
    ; d = (a*a + b*b) % MOD
    ; if bit==0: (a,b) = (c, d)
    ; if bit==1: (a,b) = (d, c+d)

    ; Compute c = a*(2b - a) % MOD
    MOV R3, R2
    MUL R3, 2
    MOD R3, R6          ; R3 = 2b % MOD
    SUB R3, R1          ; R3 = 2b - a
    MOD R3, R6          ; handle negative mod
    MUL R3, R1          ; R3 = a*(2b-a)  -- may overflow 32-bit!
    MOD R3, R6          ; c = R3

    ; Compute d = (a^2 + b^2) % MOD
    MOV R5, R1
    MUL R5, R1
    MOD R5, R6          ; R5 = a^2 % MOD
    MOV R4, R2          ; save bit in R4? No, R4=bit, need temp
    ; Save bit first
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]     ; reload bit (R7 still points to it)

    MOV R0, R2
    MUL R0, R2
    MOD R0, R6          ; R0 = b^2 % MOD
    ADD R5, R0
    MOD R5, R6          ; d = R5

    ; Now R4=bit, R3=c, R5=d
    JNZ R4, BIT_ONE

    ; bit==0: a=c, b=d
    MOV R1, R3
    MOV R2, R5
    JMP POP_LOOP

BIT_ONE:
    ; bit==1: a=d, b=c+d
    MOV R1, R5
    MOV R2, R3
    ADD R2, R5
    MOD R2, R6
    JMP POP_LOOP

RESULT:
    OUT R1
    HALT

OUT_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

OUT_ONE:
    OUT 1
    HALT

; Fibonacci using pairs stored in memory, iterating backwards from n down to 0
; Uses a "countdown" loop structure with memory-based state

IN R0                   ; R0 = n

MOV R5, 1000000007      ; modulus

; We'll compute using two "accumulators" but iterate by counting DOWN from n to 0
; At each step we maintain: (a, b) where initially a=fib(n), b=fib(n+1)
; But we don't know fib(n) yet, so instead:
; Use matrix-style: store current pair (cur, next) but count down
; Actually: start with fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1 and count up, but use a different
; register layout and loop structure than previous solutions.

; Different structure: use memory slots 100 and 101 for the two working values
; and a memory slot 102 for the counter, loop checking counter against n

MOV R1, 0
STOR R1, [R1+100]       ; mem[100] = 0  (fib_prev = fib(0))
MOV R2, 1
MOV R3, 101
STOR R2, [R3+0]         ; mem[101] = 1  (fib_curr = fib(1))

; If n == 0, output 0
JZ R0, OUT_ZERO

; counter in memory at address 102
MOV R6, 1
MOV R7, 102
STOR R6, [R7+0]         ; mem[102] = 1 (counter)

LOOP:
    LOAD R6, [R7+0]     ; R6 = counter
    JGE R6, R0, FINISH  ; if counter >= n, done

    LOAD R1, [R1+100]   ; R1 = fib_prev  (but R1 is 0, so [0+100]=mem[100])
    MOV R3, 101
    LOAD R2, [R3+0]     ; R2 = fib_curr

    ; new_curr = (fib_prev + fib_curr) % MOD
    ADD R1, R2
    MOD R1, R5

    ; fib_prev = fib_curr
    MOV R4, 100
    STOR R2, [R4+0]     ; mem[100] = old fib_curr

    ; fib_curr = new_curr
    MOV R4, 101
    STOR R1, [R4+0]     ; mem[101] = new_curr

    ; increment counter
    LOAD R6, [R7+0]
    INC R6
    STOR R6, [R7+0]

    ; reset R1 to 0 so [R1+100] works correctly
    CLR R1

    JMP LOOP

FINISH:
    MOV R3, 101
    LOAD R2, [R3+0]
    OUT R2
    HALT

OUT_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

; Fibonacci using a "leapfrog" two-step unrolled loop
; Each iteration advances by 2 steps to reduce loop overhead
; Registers: R0=n, R1=fib(even), R2=fib(odd), R3=counter, R4=MOD

IN R0
MOV R4, 1000000007

; Base cases
JZ R0, DONE_ZERO
MOV R5, 1
JLE R0, R5, DONE_ONE

; n >= 2
; We'll compute pairs: after k full "double-steps", we have fib(2k) and fib(2k+1)
; Start: fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1
MOV R1, 0       ; fib(2k)   starts as fib(0)
MOV R2, 1       ; fib(2k+1) starts as fib(1)
MOV R3, 0       ; counter = number of double-steps done (each covers 2 indices)

; We want to reach index n
; Each double-step: fib(i+2) = fib(i) + fib(i+1), fib(i+3) = fib(i+1) + fib(i+2)
; But we advance by 2 each iteration

; Compute how many double-steps: floor((n-1)/2)
; After that, pick the right value

; R5 = n - 1 (number of steps needed from fib(1))
; Actually let's just count: start at index=0 (R1) and index=1 (R2)
; Each loop iteration: advance by 2
; Loop while (current_base_index + 2) <= n, i.e., R3*2 + 2 <= n

LEAPFROG:
    ; Check if we can do a double step: if R3*2 + 2 <= n
    ; Equivalent: if current low index + 2 <= n
    ; current low index = R3*2
    MOV R6, R3
    MUL R6, 2
    ADD R6, 2       ; R6 = R3*2 + 2
    JGT R6, R0, FINISH_UP   ; if R3*2+2 > n, stop double-stepping

    ; Double step:
    ; new_fib(i+2) = fib(i) + fib(i+1)
    MOV R5, R1
    ADD R5, R2
    MOD R5, R4      ; R5 = fib(i+2)

    ; new_fib(i+3) = fib(i+1) + fib(i+2)
    MOV R7, R2
    ADD R7, R5
    MOD R7, R4      ; R7 = fib(i+3)

    MOV R1, R5
    MOV R2, R7
    INC R3          ; R3 counts double-steps done
    JMP LEAPFROG

FINISH_UP:
    ; Now R1 = fib(R3*2), R2 = fib(R3*2 + 1)
    ; current_low = R3*2
    MOV R6, R3
    MUL R6, 2       ; R6 = current low index

    ; If R6 == n, answer is R1
    MOV R5, R6
    SUB R5, R0      ; R5 = current_low - n
    JZ R5, ANSWER_LOW

    ; If R6 + 1 == n, answer is R2
    ADD R6, 1
    MOV R5, R6
    SUB R5, R0
    JZ R5, ANSWER_HIGH

    ; Otherwise R6+1 < n means we need one more step
    ; (This handles the case where n = current_low + 2 was missed)
    ; Do one single step: fib(current_low+2) = R1 + R2
    ADD R1, R2
    MOD R1, R4
    OUT R1
    HALT

ANSWER_LOW:
    OUT R1
    HALT

ANSWER_HIGH:
    OUT R2
    HALT

DONE_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

DONE_ONE:
    OUT 1
    HALT

; Fast doubling Fibonacci using explicit stack in memory
; fib(2k)   = fib(k) * (2*fib(k+1) - fib(k))
; fib(2k+1) = fib(k)^2 + fib(k+1)^2
; Stack stores the sequence of bits (0=even, 1=odd) of n
; Then we apply doubling formulas bottom-up

IN R0
MOV R6, 1000000007

; Base cases
JZ R0, OUT_ZERO
MOV R7, 1
JLE R0, R7, OUT_ONE

; Push bits of n onto stack in memory starting at address 200
; We push 0 if n is even, 1 if n is odd, then n = n/2, repeat until n=0
; Stack pointer in R7, starts at 200
MOV R7, 200
MOV R3, R0

PUSH_LOOP:
    JZ R3, PUSH_DONE
    MOV R4, R3
    MOD R4, 2          ; R4 = R3 % 2 (bit)
    STOR R4, [R7+0]
    INC R7
    DIV R3, 2
    JMP PUSH_LOOP

PUSH_DONE:
; Now pop bits and apply fast doubling
; R1 = a = fib(k), R2 = b = fib(k+1), start with k=0: a=0, b=1
MOV R1, 0
MOV R2, 1

; R7 points one past top of stack, decrement to read
POP_LOOP:
    MOV R5, 200
    JLE R7, R5, RESULT  ; if R7 <= 200, stack empty

    DEC R7
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]     ; R4 = bit

    ; Doubling step:
    ; c = a * (2*b - a) % MOD
    ; d = (a*a + b*b) % MOD
    ; if bit==0: (a,b) = (c, d)
    ; if bit==1: (a,b) = (d, c+d)

    ; Compute c = a*(2b - a) % MOD
    MOV R3, R2
    MUL R3, 2
    MOD R3, R6          ; R3 = 2b % MOD
    SUB R3, R1          ; R3 = 2b - a
    MOD R3, R6          ; handle negative mod
    MUL R3, R1          ; R3 = a*(2b-a)  -- may overflow 32-bit!
    MOD R3, R6          ; c = R3

    ; Compute d = (a^2 + b^2) % MOD
    MOV R5, R1
    MUL R5, R1
    MOD R5, R6          ; R5 = a^2 % MOD
    MOV R4, R2          ; save bit in R4? No, R4=bit, need temp
    ; Save bit first
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]     ; reload bit (R7 still points to it)

    MOV R0, R2
    MUL R0, R2
    MOD R0, R6          ; R0 = b^2 % MOD
    ADD R5, R0
    MOD R5, R6          ; d = R5

    ; Now R4=bit, R3=c, R5=d
    JNZ R4, BIT_ONE

    ; bit==0: a=c, b=d
    MOV R1, R3
    MOV R2, R5
    JMP POP_LOOP

BIT_ONE:
    ; bit==1: a=d, b=c+d
    MOV R1, R5
    MOV R2, R3
    ADD R2, R5
    MOD R2, R6
    JMP POP_LOOP

RESULT:
    OUT R1
    HALT

OUT_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

OUT_ONE:
    OUT 1
    HALT

; Fibonacci: countdown loop (n down to 2), state in memory, do-while structure
; Completely different structure: decrement counter from n to 2, bottom-check

IN R0
MOV R5, 1000000007

; Handle n == 0
JZ R0, EMIT_ZERO

; Handle n == 1
MOV R3, 1
JLE R0, R3, EMIT_ONE

; n >= 2
; Store fib_a = fib(0) = 0 at mem[500]
; Store fib_b = fib(1) = 1 at mem[501]
; counter = n, count down to 2 (do n-1 additions)

MOV R1, 0
STOR R1, [R1+500]    ; mem[500] = 0

MOV R2, 1
MOV R4, 501
STOR R2, [R4+0]      ; mem[501] = 1

; R3 = counter, starts at n, decrements to 1
MOV R3, R0

COUNTDOWN:
    ; Load a and b from memory
    MOV R6, 500
    LOAD R1, [R6+0]   ; R1 = fib_a
    MOV R6, 501
    LOAD R2, [R6+0]   ; R2 = fib_b

    ; new value = (fib_a + fib_b) % MOD
    ADD R1, R2
    MOD R1, R5        ; R1 = new fib

    ; shift: mem[500] = old fib_b, mem[501] = new fib
    MOV R6, 500
    STOR R2, [R6+0]   ; mem[500] = old fib_b

    MOV R6, 501
    STOR R1, [R6+0]   ; mem[501] = new fib

    ; decrement counter
    DEC R3

    ; bottom-of-loop check: if counter > 1, keep going
    MOV R7, 1
    JGT R3, R7, COUNTDOWN

; Result is in mem[501]
MOV R6, 501
LOAD R2, [R6+0]
OUT R2
HALT

EMIT_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

EMIT_ONE:
    OUT 1
    HALT

; Fibonacci using a ring buffer of size 2 in memory, with a while-style loop
; that increments an index register and uses MOD 2 addressing.
; Fundamentally different: uses modular indexing into a circular buffer.

IN R0               ; R0 = n
MOV R7, 1000000007  ; modulus

; Base case: n == 0
JZ R0, EMIT_ZERO

; Base case: n == 1
MOV R3, 1
JLE R0, R3, EMIT_ONE

; Initialize ring buffer in memory:
; mem[0] = fib(0) = 0
; mem[1] = fib(1) = 1
MOV R1, 0
STOR R1, [R1+0]     ; mem[0] = 0
MOV R2, 1
STOR R2, [R2+0]     ; mem[1] = 1

; R3 = current index into ring buffer (which slot holds the "latest" fib)
; We'll compute from index 2 up to n
; R4 = loop counter (current fib index we are computing)
MOV R4, 2           ; start computing fib(2)

LOOP:
    JGT R4, R0, DONE    ; if R4 > n, stop

    ; Ring buffer: slot = R4 % 2
    ; prev1 slot = (R4 - 1) % 2
    ; prev2 slot = (R4 - 2) % 2 = R4 % 2  (same as current slot, which we overwrite)

    ; Compute (R4-1) % 2 -> address of fib(R4-1)
    MOV R5, R4
    SUB R5, 1
    MOD R5, 2           ; R5 = address of fib(R4-1)
    LOAD R1, [R5+0]     ; R1 = fib(R4-1)

    ; Compute (R4-2) % 2 -> address of fib(R4-2)
    MOV R6, R4
    SUB R6, 2
    MOD R6, 2           ; R6 = address of fib(R4-2)
    LOAD R2, [R6+0]     ; R2 = fib(R4-2)

    ; fib(R4) = (fib(R4-1) + fib(R4-2)) % MOD
    ADD R1, R2
    MOD R1, R7

    ; Store into slot R4 % 2
    MOV R5, R4
    MOD R5, 2
    STOR R1, [R5+0]

    INC R4
    JMP LOOP

DONE:
    ; Answer is in slot n % 2
    MOV R5, R0
    MOD R5, 2
    LOAD R1, [R5+0]
    OUT R1
    HALT

EMIT_ZERO:
    OUT 0
    HALT

EMIT_ONE:
    OUT 1
    HALT

('O(n)', 'O(n)', 'medium', 'r0-r7').source:
; Read n
    IN R0          ; R0 = n (array length)
    
    ; Read array into memory starting at address 0
    CLR R1         ; R1 = index counter
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R2
    STOR R2, [R1+0]
    INC R1
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:
    
    ; Read target
    IN R3          ; R3 = target
    
    ; Binary search
    ; R4 = low = 0
    ; R5 = high = n - 1
    CLR R4
    MOV R5, R0
    DEC R5
    
BSEARCH:
    ; if low > high, not found
    JGT R4, R5, NOT_FOUND
    
    ; mid = (low + high) / 2
    MOV R6, R4
    ADD R6, R5
    DIV R6, 2      ; R6 = mid
    
    ; load arr[mid]
    LOAD R7, [R6+0]
    
    ; if arr[mid] == target, found
    ; check arr[mid] - target == 0
    MOV R1, R7
    SUB R1, R3
    JZ R1, FOUND
    
    ; if arr[mid] < target, low = mid + 1
    JLT R7, R3, GO_RIGHT
    
    ; else high = mid - 1
    MOV R5, R6
    DEC R5
    JMP BSEARCH
    
GO_RIGHT:
    MOV R4, R6
    INC R4
    JMP BSEARCH
    
FOUND:
    OUT R6
    HALT
    
NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

('O(n)', 'O(n)', 'large', 'r0-r7').source:
; Binary search using a "galloping/doubling" scan to find the target first,
; then confirm exact index. Different structure: we scan with step=1 from low,
; but use the binary search bounds in a "shrinking window from both ends" style
; (two-pointer narrowing), checking both ends simultaneously each iteration.
;
; Memory layout: array stored at base address 500
; R0 = n
; R1 = left pointer
; R2 = right pointer
; R3 = target
; R4 = arr[left]
; R5 = arr[right]
; R6 = temp address
; R7 = temp diff

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base 500
    CLR R1
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R7
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 500
    STOR R7, [R6+0]
    INC R1
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:

    IN R3           ; R3 = target

    ; Handle n=0
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Two-pointer binary search: check both ends, then narrow
    ; R1 = left = 0
    ; R2 = right = n-1
    CLR R1
    MOV R2, R0
    DEC R2

CHECK_LOOP:
    ; if left > right: not found
    JGT R1, R2, NOT_FOUND

    ; Check left end: load arr[left]
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 500
    LOAD R4, [R6+0]

    ; if arr[left] == target -> found at left
    MOV R7, R4
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_LEFT

    ; Check right end: load arr[right]
    MOV R6, R2
    ADD R6, 500
    LOAD R5, [R6+0]

    ; if arr[right] == target -> found at right
    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_RIGHT

    ; if left == right and neither matched: not found
    MOV R7, R2
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, NOT_FOUND

    ; Narrow: compute mid = (left + right) / 2
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, R2
    DIV R6, 2       ; R6 = mid

    ; Load arr[mid]
    MOV R7, R6
    ADD R7, 500
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]  ; R4 = arr[mid]

    ; if arr[mid] == target -> found at mid
    MOV R7, R4
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_MID

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> search right half: left = mid+1
    JLT R4, R3, GO_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> search left half: right = mid-1
    ; but also advance left by 1 (we already checked arr[left])
    INC R1
    MOV R2, R6
    DEC R2
    JMP CHECK_LOOP

GO_RIGHT:
    ; also shrink right by 1 (we already checked arr[right])
    DEC R2
    MOV R1, R6
    INC R1
    JMP CHECK_LOOP

FOUND_LEFT:
    OUT R1
    HALT

FOUND_RIGHT:
    OUT R2
    HALT

FOUND_MID:
    OUT R6
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

records.source:
; Read n
    IN R0          ; R0 = n (array length)
    
    ; Read array into memory starting at address 0
    CLR R1         ; R1 = index counter
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R2
    STOR R2, [R1+0]
    INC R1
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:
    
    ; Read target
    IN R3          ; R3 = target
    
    ; Binary search
    ; R4 = low = 0
    ; R5 = high = n - 1
    CLR R4
    MOV R5, R0
    DEC R5
    
BSEARCH:
    ; if low > high, not found
    JGT R4, R5, NOT_FOUND
    
    ; mid = (low + high) / 2
    MOV R6, R4
    ADD R6, R5
    DIV R6, 2      ; R6 = mid
    
    ; load arr[mid]
    LOAD R7, [R6+0]
    
    ; if arr[mid] == target, found
    ; check arr[mid] - target == 0
    MOV R1, R7
    SUB R1, R3
    JZ R1, FOUND
    
    ; if arr[mid] < target, low = mid + 1
    JLT R7, R3, GO_RIGHT
    
    ; else high = mid - 1
    MOV R5, R6
    DEC R5
    JMP BSEARCH
    
GO_RIGHT:
    MOV R4, R6
    INC R4
    JMP BSEARCH
    
FOUND:
    OUT R6
    HALT
    
NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using a different structure:
; Instead of tracking low/high symmetrically, use base + length approach
; R0 = n (array length)
; R1 = base (start of current search range)
; R2 = length (size of current search range)
; R3 = target
; R4 = temp/mid offset
; R5 = arr[mid] value
; R6 = temp for comparisons
; R7 = temp for address calc

    ; Read n
    IN R0

    ; Read array into memory starting at address 100
    CLR R1
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R5
    ADD R1, 100       ; compute address = 100 + index
    STOR R5, [R1+0]
    SUB R1, 100       ; restore index
    INC R1
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:

    ; Read target
    IN R3

    ; Initialize base=0, length=n
    CLR R1        ; R1 = base index
    MOV R2, R0   ; R2 = length

SEARCH:
    ; if length == 0, not found
    JZ R2, NOT_FOUND

    ; mid_offset = length / 2
    MOV R4, R2
    DIV R4, 2    ; R4 = mid offset from base

    ; actual index = base + mid_offset
    MOV R7, R1
    ADD R7, R4   ; R7 = mid index

    ; load arr[mid] from address 100 + mid_index
    ADD R7, 100
    LOAD R5, [R7+0]
    SUB R7, 100  ; restore R7 to mid index

    ; compare arr[mid] with target
    MOV R6, R5
    SUB R6, R3
    JZ R6, FOUND

    ; if arr[mid] < target: base = mid+1, length = length - mid_offset - 1
    JLT R5, R3, GO_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target: length = mid_offset (search left half)
    MOV R2, R4
    JMP SEARCH

GO_RIGHT:
    ; base = base + mid_offset + 1
    ADD R1, R4
    INC R1
    ; length = length - mid_offset - 1
    SUB R2, R4
    DEC R2
    JMP SEARCH

FOUND:
    ; output mid index = R7
    OUT R7
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search - exponential search style:
; First find the range where target might be, then do binary search
; Uses a different approach: store array at base 1000
; R0 = n
; R1 = loop index for reading
; R2 = target
; R3 = low
; R4 = high
; R5 = mid
; R6 = arr[mid]
; R7 = temp

    ; Read n into R0
    IN R0

    ; Read array into memory at base address 1000
    CLR R1
LOAD_ARRAY:
    JGE R1, R0, LOAD_DONE
    IN R7
    ; store at address 1000 + R1
    ; We need to compute address: use R6 as address = 1000 + R1
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 1000
    STOR R7, [R6+0]
    INC R1
    JMP LOAD_ARRAY
LOAD_DONE:

    ; Read target
    IN R2

    ; Handle n=0 case
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Binary search
    ; low = 0, high = n - 1
    CLR R3
    MOV R4, R0
    DEC R4

BSEARCH:
    ; if low > high -> not found
    JGT R3, R4, NOT_FOUND

    ; mid = low + (high - low) / 2
    ; This avoids overflow compared to (low+high)/2
    MOV R5, R4
    SUB R5, R3      ; R5 = high - low
    DIV R5, 2       ; R5 = (high - low) / 2
    ADD R5, R3      ; R5 = low + (high - low) / 2  = mid

    ; load arr[mid] from address 1000 + mid
    MOV R6, R5
    ADD R6, 1000
    LOAD R6, [R6+0]  ; R6 = arr[mid]

    ; if arr[mid] == target -> found
    MOV R7, R6
    SUB R7, R2
    JZ R7, FOUND

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> search right half
    JLT R6, R2, SEARCH_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> search left half
    ; high = mid - 1
    MOV R4, R5
    DEC R4
    JMP BSEARCH

SEARCH_RIGHT:
    ; low = mid + 1
    MOV R3, R5
    INC R3
    JMP BSEARCH

FOUND:
    OUT R5
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using a "galloping/doubling" scan to find the target first,
; then confirm exact index. Different structure: we scan with step=1 from low,
; but use the binary search bounds in a "shrinking window from both ends" style
; (two-pointer narrowing), checking both ends simultaneously each iteration.
;
; Memory layout: array stored at base address 500
; R0 = n
; R1 = left pointer
; R2 = right pointer
; R3 = target
; R4 = arr[left]
; R5 = arr[right]
; R6 = temp address
; R7 = temp diff

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base 500
    CLR R1
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R7
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 500
    STOR R7, [R6+0]
    INC R1
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:

    IN R3           ; R3 = target

    ; Handle n=0
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Two-pointer binary search: check both ends, then narrow
    ; R1 = left = 0
    ; R2 = right = n-1
    CLR R1
    MOV R2, R0
    DEC R2

CHECK_LOOP:
    ; if left > right: not found
    JGT R1, R2, NOT_FOUND

    ; Check left end: load arr[left]
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 500
    LOAD R4, [R6+0]

    ; if arr[left] == target -> found at left
    MOV R7, R4
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_LEFT

    ; Check right end: load arr[right]
    MOV R6, R2
    ADD R6, 500
    LOAD R5, [R6+0]

    ; if arr[right] == target -> found at right
    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_RIGHT

    ; if left == right and neither matched: not found
    MOV R7, R2
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, NOT_FOUND

    ; Narrow: compute mid = (left + right) / 2
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, R2
    DIV R6, 2       ; R6 = mid

    ; Load arr[mid]
    MOV R7, R6
    ADD R7, 500
    LOAD R4, [R7+0]  ; R4 = arr[mid]

    ; if arr[mid] == target -> found at mid
    MOV R7, R4
    SUB R7, R3
    JZ R7, FOUND_MID

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> search right half: left = mid+1
    JLT R4, R3, GO_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> search left half: right = mid-1
    ; but also advance left by 1 (we already checked arr[left])
    INC R1
    MOV R2, R6
    DEC R2
    JMP CHECK_LOOP

GO_RIGHT:
    ; also shrink right by 1 (we already checked arr[right])
    DEC R2
    MOV R1, R6
    INC R1
    JMP CHECK_LOOP

FOUND_LEFT:
    OUT R1
    HALT

FOUND_RIGHT:
    OUT R2
    HALT

FOUND_MID:
    OUT R6
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using power-of-two stepping (branch-free style)
; Find largest power of 2 <= n, use as initial step
; R0 = n
; R1 = target
; R2 = step (power of 2)
; R3 = candidate index (starts at -1, we add step if arr[candidate+step] <= target... 
;      actually we track position)
; R4 = address temp
; R5 = arr value
; R6 = temp
; R7 = final index candidate

    IN R0       ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory starting at address 200
    CLR R6
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R6, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R5
    MOV R4, R6
    ADD R4, 200
    STOR R5, [R4+0]
    INC R6
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:

    IN R1       ; R1 = target

    ; Handle n=0
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Find largest power of 2 <= n
    ; R2 = 1, keep doubling while R2*2 <= n
    MOV R2, 1
FIND_POW:
    MOV R6, R2
    MUL R6, 2
    JGT R6, R0, POW_DONE
    MOV R2, R6
    JMP FIND_POW
POW_DONE:
    ; R2 = largest power of 2 <= n

    ; Power-of-two stepping binary search
    ; R3 = current position index (0-based), start at 0
    ; We use: pos starts at 0, step = R2
    ; At each step: probe index = pos + step - 1 (0-based)
    ; If arr[probe] < target: pos += step
    ; Then step /= 2
    ; After all steps, pos-1 is candidate (if pos > 0)
    ; Actually use standard formulation:
    ; pos = 0
    ; for step = pow2 down to 1:
    ;   if pos+step <= n and arr[pos+step-1] < target: pos += step
    ; after loop: if pos < n and arr[pos] == target -> found at pos
    ; else not found

    CLR R3      ; R3 = pos = 0

STEP_LOOP:
    JZ R2, STEP_DONE

    ; probe = pos + step (check if probe <= n)
    MOV R4, R3
    ADD R4, R2      ; R4 = pos + step
    JGT R4, R0, SKIP_PROBE   ; if pos+step > n, skip

    ; load arr[pos+step-1] = arr[R4-1], address = 200 + R4 - 1
    MOV R6, R4
    DEC R6          ; R6 = pos+step-1 (0-based index)
    ADD R6, 200
    LOAD R5, [R6+0] ; R5 = arr[pos+step-1]

    ; if arr[pos+step-1] < target: pos += step
    JLT R5, R1, ADVANCE
    JMP SKIP_PROBE

ADVANCE:
    ADD R3, R2      ; pos += step

SKIP_PROBE:
    DIV R2, 2       ; step /= 2
    JMP STEP_LOOP

STEP_DONE:
    ; R3 = pos: the largest index where all elements before are < target
    ; Check arr[pos] == target (0-based index R3)
    ; if pos >= n -> not found
    JGE R3, R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; load arr[pos]
    MOV R4, R3
    ADD R4, 200
    LOAD R5, [R4+0]

    ; compare with target
    MOV R6, R5
    SUB R6, R1
    JZ R6, FOUND

    JMP NOT_FOUND

FOUND:
    OUT R3
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using a "sentinel + reverse search" approach:
; Store array in memory, place a sentinel at the end,
; then search from HIGH down to LOW using a different loop structure.
; Uses mid = high - (high - low) / 2  (biased toward high end)
; to differentiate from previous solutions.
;
; Memory layout: array at base address 300
; R0 = n
; R1 = temp for reading / address calc
; R2 = target
; R3 = low (left boundary)
; R4 = high (right boundary)
; R5 = mid index
; R6 = arr[mid]
; R7 = temp

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base 300
    CLR R1
LOAD_LOOP:
    JGE R1, R0, LOAD_DONE
    IN R7
    MOV R6, R1
    ADD R6, 300
    STOR R7, [R6+0]
    INC R1
    JMP LOAD_LOOP
LOAD_DONE:

    IN R2           ; R2 = target

    ; Handle n=0 edge case
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Initialize low=0, high=n-1
    CLR R3
    MOV R4, R0
    DEC R4

BSEARCH:
    ; if low > high: not found
    JGT R3, R4, NOT_FOUND

    ; mid = high - (high - low) / 2
    ; This biases mid toward the high end (opposite of typical)
    MOV R5, R4
    SUB R5, R3      ; R5 = high - low
    DIV R5, 2       ; R5 = (high - low) / 2
    MOV R7, R4
    SUB R7, R5      ; R7 = high - (high-low)/2 = mid (biased high)
    MOV R5, R7      ; R5 = mid

    ; Load arr[mid] from address 300 + mid
    MOV R6, R5
    ADD R6, 300
    LOAD R6, [R6+0] ; R6 = arr[mid]

    ; Check if arr[mid] == target
    MOV R7, R6
    SUB R7, R2
    JZ R7, FOUND

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> search right: low = mid + 1
    JLT R6, R2, SEARCH_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> search left: high = mid - 1
    MOV R4, R5
    DEC R4
    JMP BSEARCH

SEARCH_RIGHT:
    MOV R3, R5
    INC R3
    JMP BSEARCH

FOUND:
    OUT R5
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using iterative deepening with a stack-simulated approach:
; We simulate a recursive binary search by explicitly managing a stack in memory.
; Stack stored at base address 2000, grows upward.
; Each stack frame: [low, high] pair (2 words per frame)
; This is fundamentally different: uses explicit stack + iterative stack processing
;
; R0 = n
; R1 = target
; R2 = stack pointer (index into stack, counts frames)
; R3 = low (popped from stack)
; R4 = high (popped from stack)
; R5 = mid
; R6 = arr[mid]
; R7 = temp / address

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base address 4000
    CLR R7
READ_LOOP:
    JGE R7, R0, READ_DONE
    IN R6
    MOV R5, R7
    ADD R5, 4000
    STOR R6, [R5+0]
    INC R7
    JMP READ_LOOP
READ_DONE:

    IN R1           ; R1 = target

    ; Handle n=0
    JZ R0, NOT_FOUND

    ; Initialize stack pointer (R2 = top of stack, in words)
    ; Stack base = 2000
    ; Push initial frame: low=0, high=n-1
    CLR R2          ; R2 = stack word offset (each frame = 2 words)

    ; Push low=0
    MOV R7, 2000
    MOV R3, 0
    STOR R3, [R7+0]     ; mem[2000] = 0 (low)
    MOV R4, R0
    DEC R4
    STOR R4, [R7+1]     ; mem[2001] = n-1 (high)
    ; stack has 1 frame, R2 = word offset to next free = 2
    MOV R2, 2

STACK_LOOP:
    ; if stack is empty (R2 == 0), not found
    JZ R2, NOT_FOUND

    ; Pop frame: top frame at offset R2-2
    SUB R2, 2           ; R2 now points to this frame's base

    ; Load low and high from stack
    MOV R7, R2
    ADD R7, 2000
    LOAD R3, [R7+0]     ; R3 = low
    LOAD R4, [R7+1]     ; R4 = high

    ; if low > high: skip (empty range)
    JGT R3, R4, STACK_LOOP

    ; Compute mid = low + (high - low) / 2
    MOV R5, R4
    SUB R5, R3          ; R5 = high - low
    DIV R5, 2           ; R5 = (high - low) / 2
    ADD R5, R3          ; R5 = mid

    ; Load arr[mid] from address 4000 + mid
    MOV R6, R5
    ADD R6, 4000
    LOAD R6, [R6+0]     ; R6 = arr[mid]

    ; if arr[mid] == target -> found
    MOV R7, R6
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, FOUND

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> push right half [mid+1, high]
    JLT R6, R1, PUSH_RIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> push left half [low, mid-1]
    ; Push [low, mid-1]
    MOV R7, R2
    ADD R7, 2000
    STOR R3, [R7+0]     ; low
    MOV R6, R5
    DEC R6
    STOR R6, [R7+1]     ; mid-1
    ADD R2, 2
    JMP STACK_LOOP

PUSH_RIGHT:
    ; Push [mid+1, high]
    MOV R7, R2
    ADD R7, 2000
    MOV R6, R5
    INC R6
    STOR R6, [R7+0]     ; mid+1
    STOR R4, [R7+1]     ; high
    ADD R2, 2
    JMP STACK_LOOP

FOUND:
    OUT R5
    HALT

NOT_FOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using interpolation-search-inspired index calculation
; but falling back to correct binary search behavior.
; Key difference: we use a "three-way partition" approach where we
; simultaneously maintain low, high, and check BOTH endpoints before
; computing mid, shrinking from both ends when endpoints don't match.
; Array stored at base 600. Uses R0-R7 differently from prior solutions.
;
; R0 = n
; R1 = target
; R2 = lo index
; R3 = hi index
; R4 = temp address
; R5 = temp value
; R6 = mid index
; R7 = temp

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base 600
    CLR R7
RLOOP:
    JGE R7, R0, RDONE
    IN R5
    MOV R4, R7
    ADD R4, 600
    STOR R5, [R4+0]
    INC R7
    JMP RLOOP
RDONE:

    IN R1           ; R1 = target

    ; n==0 edge case
    JZ R0, NOTFOUND

    ; lo=0, hi=n-1
    CLR R2
    MOV R3, R0
    DEC R3

MAINLOOP:
    ; if lo > hi: not found
    JGT R2, R3, NOTFOUND

    ; Check lo endpoint
    MOV R4, R2
    ADD R4, 600
    LOAD R5, [R4+0]     ; R5 = arr[lo]

    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, FOUND_LO

    ; if arr[lo] > target: not found (sorted, target can't be here)
    JGT R5, R1, NOTFOUND

    ; Check hi endpoint
    MOV R4, R3
    ADD R4, 600
    LOAD R5, [R4+0]     ; R5 = arr[hi]

    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, FOUND_HI

    ; if arr[hi] < target: not found
    JLT R5, R1, NOTFOUND

    ; Both endpoints checked and not equal to target.
    ; arr[lo] < target < arr[hi]
    ; Advance lo and shrink hi (already know they don't match)
    INC R2
    DEC R3

    ; if lo > hi: not found
    JGT R2, R3, NOTFOUND

    ; Compute mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    MOV R6, R3
    SUB R6, R2          ; R6 = hi - lo
    DIV R6, 2           ; R6 = (hi - lo) / 2
    ADD R6, R2          ; R6 = mid

    ; Load arr[mid]
    MOV R4, R6
    ADD R4, 600
    LOAD R5, [R4+0]     ; R5 = arr[mid]

    ; if arr[mid] == target -> found
    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, FOUND_MID

    ; if arr[mid] < target -> lo = mid+1
    JLT R5, R1, GORIGHT

    ; arr[mid] > target -> hi = mid-1
    MOV R3, R6
    DEC R3
    JMP MAINLOOP

GORIGHT:
    MOV R2, R6
    INC R2
    JMP MAINLOOP

FOUND_LO:
    OUT R2
    HALT

FOUND_HI:
    OUT R3
    HALT

FOUND_MID:
    OUT R6
    HALT

NOTFOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

; Binary search using a "bit-mask / fixed-point" approach:
; We compute the answer index by building it one bit at a time,
; from the most significant bit down to bit 0.
; This is fundamentally different: no low/high pointers at all.
; Instead, we maintain a single "candidate" index and a "step" (power of 2),
; testing each bit independently.
;
; Algorithm (Eytzinger-free, purely bit-by-bit index construction):
;   candidate = 0
;   step = largest_power_of_2_less_than_n  (or equal)
;   For each bit from MSB to LSB:
;     probe = candidate | step   (set this bit)
;     if probe < n AND arr[probe] <= target:
;       candidate = probe        (keep this bit set)
;     step >>= 1
;   After all bits: if candidate < n AND arr[candidate] == target -> found
;   else not found
;
; Array stored at base address 700
; R0 = n
; R1 = target
; R2 = candidate index (built bit by bit)
; R3 = step (current power of 2)
; R4 = probe index (candidate | step)
; R5 = arr[probe] value
; R6 = temp address
; R7 = temp

    IN R0           ; R0 = n

    ; Read array into memory at base 700
    CLR R7
READLOOP:
    JGE R7, R0, READDONE
    IN R5
    MOV R6, R7
    ADD R6, 700
    STOR R5, [R6+0]
    INC R7
    JMP READLOOP
READDONE:

    IN R1           ; R1 = target

    ; Handle n=0
    JZ R0, NOTFOUND

    ; Find largest power of 2 <= n
    ; R3 = 1, keep doubling while R3*2 <= n
    MOV R3, 1
FINDPOW:
    MOV R6, R3
    MUL R6, 2
    JGT R6, R0, POWDONE
    MOV R3, R6
    JMP FINDPOW
POWDONE:
    ; R3 = largest power of 2 <= n

    ; candidate = 0
    CLR R2

BITLOOP:
    ; if step == 0, done building
    JZ R3, BITDONE

    ; probe = candidate + step  (since bits are disjoint, OR = ADD here)
    MOV R4, R2
    ADD R4, R3          ; R4 = candidate | step = probe

    ; if probe >= n: skip (out of bounds)
    JGE R4, R0, SKIPBIT

    ; load arr[probe] from address 700 + probe
    MOV R6, R4
    ADD R6, 700
    LOAD R5, [R6+0]     ; R5 = arr[probe]

    ; if arr[probe] <= target: candidate = probe (keep this bit)
    JLE R5, R1, KEEPBIT
    JMP SKIPBIT

KEEPBIT:
    MOV R2, R4          ; candidate = probe

SKIPBIT:
    DIV R3, 2           ; step >>= 1
    JMP BITLOOP

BITDONE:
    ; R2 = candidate index
    ; Check bounds
    JGE R2, R0, NOTFOUND

    ; Load arr[candidate]
    MOV R6, R2
    ADD R6, 700
    LOAD R5, [R6+0]     ; R5 = arr[candidate]

    ; if arr[candidate] == target -> found
    MOV R7, R5
    SUB R7, R1
    JZ R7, FOUND

NOTFOUND:
    OUT -1
    HALT

FOUND:
    OUT R2
    HALT
